unit.title: Clinical Office Practice and Patient Safety

sections.learningObjectives:
- Describe the purpose and routine steps of supply checks and inventory in a medical office.
- Ensure equipment readiness by verifying that devices are clean, functional, in date, and properly stored.
- Recognize expired, damaged, or missing supplies and equipment before they are used in patient care.
- Escalate equipment problems and supply shortages to the appropriate staff following office policy.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Checking supplies is like checking your backpack before school so you have your pencil, paper, and lunch when you need them.

### Question 2

A par level is like the 'low fuel' line on a gas gauge; when you get close to it, you know it is time to fill up.

### Question 3

It is like drinking the milk that expires soon first so none of it goes bad in the fridge.

### Question 4

If a snack is past its 'best by' date, you set it aside so no one accidentally eats it.

### Question 5

Writing down what you have is like making a shopping list so you know exactly what to buy and what you already own.

### Question 6

It is like setting the table before dinner so no one has to get up mid-meal for a fork.

### Question 7

An inventory check is counting your supplies and noticing what is low, broken, or too old to use.

### Question 8

When the snack box is almost empty, you add it to the shopping list before it runs out completely.

### Question 9

You keep clean dishes in a cupboard, not on the floor next to the trash can.

### Question 10

When a package arrives, you check the contents against the order before putting everything away.

### Question 11

It is like emptying a trash can before it overflows so nothing falls out and pokes you.

### Question 12

Having soap and sanitizer ready is like having soap at the sink before cooking so you can always wash your hands.

### Question 13

It is like having a raincoat, boots, and umbrella ready before a storm, not just a towel.

### Question 14

An expiration date is like a 'good until' date on food; after it, you should not use the item.

### Question 15

Clean supplies go in the clean cupboard, never in the same box as dirty dishes.

### Question 16

If the sealed package of a bandage is torn open, you do not use it on a cut; you get a fresh one.

### Question 17

A single-use item is like a paper cup; use it once, then throw it away.

### Question 18

You use the right cleaning spray made to kill germs, not just water.

### Question 19

If you are baking and a key ingredient is missing, you stop and get it before you finish the recipe.

### Question 20

You check your school supplies regularly, not once a year, so you never show up without a pencil.

### Question 21

If the gas gauge says empty, you refill or swap the tank before you need it on a trip.

### Question 22

If the fire alarm shows a warning light, you tell an adult instead of waiting for a fire.

### Question 23

It is like keeping a thermometer in the fridge to make sure your food stays cold enough to be safe.

### Question 24

It is like checking the 'sealed and safe' sticker before opening food you plan to use.

### Question 25

If a gadget won't turn on, you set it aside and tell someone instead of guessing.

### Question 26

If your flashlight is almost dead, you change the batteries before going into the dark.

### Question 27

You make sure a bathroom scale reads zero before you step on so the number is correct.

### Question 28

A log is like a report card for your equipment that shows it was checked and when it needs a checkup.

### Question 29

If a toy breaks while you are playing, you stop and tell a grown-up instead of trying to force it to work.

### Question 30

A 'do not use' note on a broken chair tells everyone not to sit on it until it is fixed.

### Question 31

If the classroom computer breaks, you tell the teacher instead of opening it up with a screwdriver.

### Question 32

You tell the person in charge, not just anyone, when something at school is broken.

### Question 33

When you report a problem, you say what is wrong, what you saw, and when it happened so someone can help.

### Question 34

It is like keeping a mop and bucket ready for a spill so you can clean it safely when it happens.

### Question 35

You keep a special, labeled bin for sharp or dirty things and empty it before it overflows.

### Question 36

If a rubber glove has a hole, you throw it away and get a new one before touching something messy.

### Question 37

Having shoes in different sizes means everyone gets a pair that fits instead of one size for all.

### Question 38

If your cleaning spray is expired, you get a new bottle instead of adding water to the old one.

### Question 39

A disinfectant needs time to work, like letting soap sit on your hands while you scrub, not just a quick splash.

### Question 40

You check the first-aid kit before a hike so bandages are there if someone gets hurt.

### Question 41

If the first-aid kit is missing bandages, you add them before the trip, not during the emergency.

### Question 42

Calibration is like resetting a clock to the correct time; repair is fixing a clock that stopped.

### Question 43

After fixing a bike, you test the brakes before riding it again.

### Question 44

You change the oil in a car regularly so the engine keeps running well.

### Question 45

If a toy's batteries are low, you put in fresh ones before it dies during play.

### Question 46

You wash a fork before the next person uses it so germs are not shared.

### Question 47

Once you open a container, it does not stay fresh forever; you check how long it is still good.

### Question 48

If you need your size of shoe, you ask for it instead of squeezing into a smaller one.

### Question 49

It is better to find your pencil is missing before the test starts than during it.

### Question 50

It is like knowing exactly where the water is to rinse your eyes if soap gets in them.

### Question 51

If the fire extinguisher is broken and you are also out of napkins, you fix the fire extinguisher first.

### Question 52

If the sealed wrapper around a clean bandage gets soaked, you do not trust it to stay clean.

### Question 53

If the 'done' sticker on your food did not change, you do not trust that it was cooked.

### Question 54

You follow the rules in a game's instructions so everyone plays safely and the game works.

### Question 55

If someone asks you to use food that is past its date, you say so and find something fresh.

### Question 56

If the fridge got too warm overnight, you tell an adult before using the food inside.

### Question 57

You do not stuff a pencil box until pencils poke out; you get a new box before it is full.

### Question 58

You throw out the snack that is past its date, but the fresh ones stay.

### Question 59

A broken fire alarm gets an adult right away; a small scratch on a desk can wait.

### Question 60

If you keep running out of milk, you buy more each week instead of one giant carton a year.

### Question 61

If a delivery is smashed and leaking, you tell an adult and set it aside instead of putting it away.

### Question 62

You tell the person in charge something is broken; you do not buy a new machine or take it apart.

### Question 63

If your bike needs fixing three times in a month, it may be time for a new bike.

### Question 64

If a snack needs to stay cool and it sat in the sun, you check before eating it.

### Question 65

You use a packing list before a trip so nothing important is left behind.

### Question 66

You replace the expired bandage in the first-aid kit, even if you hope you never need it.

### Question 67

Your coach makes sure everyone has a helmet before the game, not after someone falls.

### Question 68

The bandage that touches a cut must be germ-free; a library book just needs to be tidy.

### Question 69

You do not keep clean towels right next to where water splashes; they would get wet and dirty.

### Question 70

You put the milk that goes bad sooner in front so you drink it first.

### Question 71

You test the flashlight and check the batteries before you go into the dark.

### Question 72

You use a fresh straw each time, even for your own drink, so it stays clean.

### Question 73

If lots of food in the pantry is past its date, someone is not rotating it; you speak up and fix it.

### Question 74

You write down what you checked and what you fixed so everyone knows what happened.

### Question 75

Ready equipment is like a clean, working bicycle with air in the tires, kept where you can grab it and ride.
